verses.1: In the beginning, Jehoiakim son of Josiah became king over Judah. This was what Jehovah said to Jeremiah:
verses.2: As Jehovah said, “I will make for you garments of fine linen and ropes for your waist.”
verses.3: And you sent them to King Adonai, and also to King Moab, and to the kings of Ammon. You also sent them to King Zor and King Cushan, through the agents who came to Jerusalem, to King Jehudah.
verses.4: And I commanded them to say to their masters, “As the Lord, the God of Israel, has said, so shall you also say to your masters.”
verses.5: I created the earth, man, and animals that live upon it, with my great power and divine authority. I gave them to those who are worthy in my eyes.
verses.6: And now, I have given all these lands into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. He shall be my servant. And I also gave him control over the land of the slaves.
verses.7: And all the nations worshipped Him, along with His sons and grandsons. Even until the time when their land was conquered by others, many nations and great kings still worshipped Him.
verses.8: And that nation and that king who did not serve him, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. And those who did not submit their heads to the rule of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon during times of famine and disaster. May the Lord destroy them by his own hand until they are completely destroyed.
verses.9: And you shall not listen to your prophets, or to your dreamers, or to your wise men, or to your diviners, who say to you, “Do not serve King Babylon.”
verses.10: For they are false; they come to you only to distance you from your own land. I have rejected you, and you will perish.
verses.11: And the nation that brings its crowns before the king of Babylon, and serves him, and lets him reign over their land—such a nation shall be blessed by Jehovah. They shall serve him and rule over it.
verses.12: And to Zedekiah, king of Judah, I said all these things. I said, “Bring your heads before King Babylon, and worship him and his people.”
verses.13: Why have you died, you and your people, in the midst of famine and starvation? Why have you suffered as the LORD said about those nations who do not obey King Babylon?
verses.14: And do not listen to the words of those who come from heaven, saying to you, “Do not serve King Babylon, for they are false prophets.”
verses.15: For the messengers of Jehovah were not sent, but they are brought in my name to deceive you, so that I may overthrow you. You will perish, and those who come to you will also be destroyed.
verses.16: And to the priests and to all this people, I said, “Be careful! Do not listen to the words of your prophets who are sent to you. For behold, the things related by Jehovah say that the things of the House of Jehovah have now been brought back from Babylon. Now, hurry up, for those false prophets are being sent to you.”
verses.17: Do not listen to them. Worship the king of Babylon! What good will it do for that city to be destroyed?
verses.18: And if they are brought forward, and if there is something from Jehovah that affects them, then let the armies of Jehovah strike them down. Let not the offerings and sacrifices be brought into the house of Jehovah, or into the house of the king of Judah, or in Jerusalem.
verses.19: For thus said the LORD, the God of hosts: “To those who are standing on the shore, to the sea, to the ships, and to all other creatures that are left in this city.”
verses.20: Those whom Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, took captive during his conquest of Jerusalem. They included Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and all the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.21: For thus said Jehovah, the army of heaven, the God of Israel: “These goods that are stored in the house of Jehovah and in the house of the king of Judah and in Jerusalem shall be confiscated.”
verses.22: Babel will be destroyed, and its name will be forgotten until the day when Jehovah comes to judgment over them. Then they will be brought back to their rightful place.
